newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor's son drew phantom Air France salary.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor's son drew phantom Air France salary.

text.p: The son of Paris mayor Jean Tiberi received a disputed 1.1 million francs ($220,000) in pay from state airline Air France after he stopped working for the company, a cabinet minister said.

Minister for Relations with Parliament Roger Romani said in a statement late on Thursday the government reimbursed the sum paid to Dominique Tiberi for almost three years from 1993 when he began his employment as an aide in Romani's cabinet.
Romani said the payment was made when Air France pointed out the anomaly.
Dominique Tiberi was officially taken on to the cabinet payroll from 1996. He told the newspaper Le Monde he received no government pay while drawing the Air France salary.

The latest controversy involving the Tiberi family was first reported by the daily on Thursday. It said Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office reimbursed Air France in June only when a police inquiry was opened into the payments.
The airline told Reuters it was long common practice for senior employees of state firms to continue to be paid by them when seconded to other government tasks.
Romani's statement said the Tiberi case was different from some cases in the 1980s when Air France paid salaries to some people in ministerial cabinets as a political favour.

Dominique Tiberi's father Jean has been buffeted for months by charges that funds were channelled to the ruling Rally for the Republic (RPR) party by contractors working for the Paris town hall when President Jacques Chirac was mayor and Tiberi his deputy.

Father and son were also the target of a probe about the conditions under which the younger Tiberi, and his sister, were attributed large city-owned flats for low rents even though they already owned flats which they then rented.
The mayor's wife, Dominique Tiberi's mother, is herself at the centre of a probe for possible excessive payments by a local authority for a brief report she drew up for them.
France is in the throes of investigations for politically-linked corruption which have affected both left and right-wing parties.
